learn.title: Division with whole numbers
learn.body: When both sides of `/` are ints, C divides and throws away the fractional part. So `7 / 2` is 3, not 3.5. It drops the decimals, it does not round. This surprises almost every beginner.

learn.title: The modulo operator
learn.body: `%` gives the remainder after division. `7 % 2` is 1, because 7 is three twos plus 1 left over. It only works on integers. In a format string `%` is something else, so do not confuse the two.

learn.title: See both
learn.body: The middle line uses 2.0, a decimal, so C does real division.

learn.title: Getting a decimal answer
learn.body: If either side is a decimal, the division is done with decimals. `7 / 2.0` is 3.5. You can also convert with a cast: `(double) 7 / 2` turns the 7 into a double first, so the result is 3.5.

learn.title: What modulo is good for
learn.body: `n % 2 == 0` tests for even. `n % 10` is the last digit. `n / 10` removes the last digit. Time works too: 135 minutes is `135 / 60` hours and `135 % 60` minutes.

learn.title: 135 minutes in hours
learn.body: Split 135 minutes into hours and minutes.
steps: Hours: `135 / 60` is 2, because 60 fits into 135 twice
So 135 minutes is 2 hours and 15 minutes

learn.body: Dividing by zero is not allowed. With ints it is undefined behaviour, so check the divisor first.
